facts: The NetWare Core Protocol (NCP) is a network protocol.
The NetWare Core Protocol is used in some products from Novell, Inc.
The NetWare Core Protocol is usually associated with the client-server operating system Novell NetWare.
Novell NetWare originally supported primarily MS-DOS client stations.
Support for Microsoft Windows was added to Novell NetWare.
Support for the classic Mac OS was added to Novell NetWare.
Support for Linux was added to Novell NetWare.
Support for Windows NT was added to Novell NetWare.
Support for various flavors of Unix was added to Novell NetWare.
The NetWare Core Protocol is used to access remote command execution.
The NetWare Core Protocol is used to access clock synchronization.
The NetWare Core Protocol is used to access messaging.
The NetWare Core Protocol originally took advantage of an easy network configuration of the IPX/SPX protocol stack.
Since mid-1990s the TCP/IP implementation is available.
Novell eDirectory uses NCP for synchronizing data changes between the servers in a directory service tree.
